summary.text: Influenza A virus, or IAV, is a pathogen whose strains cause seasonal flu in humans and can also infect birds and some mammals.
Its subtypes are defined by the combination of two surface proteins, hemagglutinin (H) and neuraminidase (N), as in H1N1.
The virus changes through mutation and genetic reassortment, which lets it evade immunity and sometimes jump between species.

facts.label: Notable pandemic
facts.value: The Spanish Flu pandemic of 1918 to 1920

facts.label: Known protein types
facts.value: 18 types of hemagglutinin and 11 of neuraminidase

facts.label: Global monitoring
facts.value: GISRS tests specimens through labs in 127 countries

items.prompt: A flu sample is labeled H5N1. What do those characters tell you?

options.label: Five hosts it has infected, and one of them human
A type-5 hemagglutinin and a type-1 neuraminidase on its surface
The fifth of eight genome segments and the first of eleven
Five years since its first sighting and one since the last

items.explain: H5N1 designates a subtype with a type-5 hemagglutinin protein and a type-1 neuraminidase protein.

items.prompt: Why can't one flu vaccine recipe be used year after year?

options.label: The virus keeps changing, so vaccines must be reformulated to keep up
A new species of influenza A appears each year
Vaccines wear out in storage over a few months
The immune system forgets a vaccine every winter

items.explain: IAV vaccines need to be reformulated regularly to keep up with changes in the virus, which changes through mutation and reassortment.

items.prompt: A sample is named A/Rio de Janeiro/62434/2021, with no animal field. From what was it collected by default?

options.label: A pig
A wild bird
A bat
A human

items.explain: When no species is mentioned in the name, the sample was by default collected from a human.

items.prompt: Some aquatic birds show no symptoms from a bird-adapted strain. What could happen if it reaches a chicken farm?

options.label: It would stay harmless, as it is in the ducks
It would be unable to infect chickens
It could be lethal to the chickens
It would turn into seasonal human flu

items.explain: Bird-adapted strains can be asymptomatic in some aquatic birds but lethal if they spread to other species, such as chickens.

items.prompt: On a poultry farm, what do experts prefer to vaccination for controlling IAV disease?

options.label: Biosecurity measures such as quarantine, segregation and good hygiene
Treating birds early with antiviral medicines
Letting the flock mix with wild birds
Housing the poultry beside pigs

items.explain: Vaccination can prevent IAV disease in poultry, but biosecurity control measures such as quarantine, segregation and good hygiene are preferred.

items.prompt: Which two proteins stick out like spikes from the influenza envelope and can trigger antibodies?

options.label: PB1 and PB2
Hemagglutinin and neuraminidase
The nucleoprotein and M1
M2 and PA

items.explain: Hemagglutinin and neuraminidase are inserted into the envelope as spikes, and both are antigenic.
